- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive and recent highs are followed by a spike; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% after a strong upward sentiment surge.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or shows strong downward momentum; add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- Forecast tends to lag in the first 5–7 days after a sharp price drop; adjust upward by 1–3% for the first 3–5 days post-negative sentiment.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, forecast often overshoots the true value; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.30) and price is rising, reduce forecast by 2–5% in the next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, forecast often underestimates the drop; add 1–3% to forecast to reflect sentiment-driven volatility.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong downward sentiment, reduce forecast by 3–6% to account for potential mean reversion or sentiment-driven correction.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +0.20 to -0.20), reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
